name: LSASS Memory
description: Adversaries may attempt to access credential material stored in the process memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service.

name: System Network Configuration Discovery
description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings of systems they access.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Adversaries may use RDP to log into a system using valid accounts.

name: SSH
description: Adversaries may use SSH to move laterally within an environment.

name: System Owner/User Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to identify the primary user or currently logged-in user.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation
description: Adversaries may abuse WMI to execute malicious commands and payloads.

name: System Network Connections Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to obtain a listing of network connections to or from the compromised system.

name: Scheduled Task/Job
description: Adversaries may abuse Windows Task Scheduler to execute programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis.

name: PowerShell
description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

name: Windows Command Shell
description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell for execution.

name: Unix Shell
description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution.

name: Python
description: Adversaries may abuse Python commands and scripts for execution.

name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
description: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding programs to a startup folder or referencing them with registry run keys.

name: Clear Windows Event Logs
description: Adversaries may clear Windows event logs to hide activity.

name: Local Account
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of local system accounts.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.

name: Modify Registry
description: Adversaries may interact with the Windows Registry to hide configuration information or establish persistence.

name: Mshta
description: Adversaries may abuse mshta.exe to proxy execution of malicious files or scripts.

name: Rundll32
description: Adversaries may abuse rundll32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

name: Impair Defenses
description: Adversaries may maliciously modify components of a victim environment to hinder defensive mechanisms.
